task_design_assessment.overall: Reasonable borrowing for a development QA benchmark, especially causal evidence and reproducibility; not yet a broad workload benchmark.

tasks.kind: Why/how: filtering semantics and candidate-state handoff
Why/how: row/key mapping and maintenance branch selection

shared_strengths: User-visible symptoms rather than fix locations; pre-fix snapshots hide solution and history.
Explicit causal units, equivalent valid source allowed, citations must support claims rather than merely overlap.
Gold, repair and regression principles remain evaluator-only; runtime reproduction limitations and contamination risk disclosed.
limits: All three are one-repository causal bug explanations requiring repair/test discussion, not symbol lookup or general architecture coverage. This is acceptable for a named closed-issue causal-QA subset but must not imply all repository QA.
Exact pre-fix failure and post-fix success are not experimentally validated; static evidence can support code reasoning but not a claim that every described runtime scenario was reproduced.
One pair per task is development evidence; task repeats and independently selected tasks answer different questions.

secondary: Tool calls, actual zg use and failures
primary_vs_secondary.interpretation: Quality improvement and efficiency improvement are distinct possible benefits. A valid higher-quality answer at higher cost is a quality/resource tradeoff, not no benefit and not an unconditional efficiency win. Equal-quality lower-cost answers can support an efficiency signal. Both failing a source-grounded gate cannot be turned into successful-QA evidence by a higher numeric score.
primary_vs_secondary.must_not_redefine: Keep existing frozen success rules and all outcomes. If a phase also preregistered a joint efficiency signal, evaluate it as written; do not retroactively relax that phase. Future phase objectives can separately preregister quality-first and efficiency-first endpoints.
